blocks.text: When a potential difference V is applied across the ends of a conductor, a current I starts flowing through it.

blocks.title: Ohm's law
blocks.text: The current flowing through a conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference applied across the conductor, provided there is no change in the physical state of the conductor. Mathematically V is proportional to I, or V = RI ... (9.31).
Here R is a constant known as the resistance of the conductor. The SI unit of resistance is the ohm, denoted by the Greek capital letter omega.

blocks.title: One ohm
blocks.text: The resistance of a conductor is 1 ohm if a current of 1 ampere flows through it when a potential difference of 1 volt is applied across its ends.
